references.text: Peter testifies that the apostles ate and drank with Jesus after his resurrection from the dead, confirming the physical reality of the resurrection ([ref:Apg 10:41|Acts 10:41]).
Jesus gathered with the disciples after the resurrection and shared a meal with them, emphasizing his bodily presence ([ref:Apg 1:4|Acts 1:4]).

At the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus ate with the disciples after the resurrection. Jesus took bread and gave it to them, and likewise fish – further confirmation of his bodily resurrection ([ref:Joh 21:12-13|John 21:12-13]).

Earlier in the same chapter, Jesus broke bread with the travelers on the road to Emmaus, and then their eyes were opened. The meal serves as a sign of recognition for the risen one ([ref:Luk 24:30-31|Luke 24:30-31]).

Immediately before this, Jesus asked for something to eat and was given a piece of grilled fish, which he then ate in front of the disciples to show that he is not a spirit ([ref:Luk 24:41-42|Luke 24:41-42]).
